newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Steady in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Steady in quiet market.

text.p: Singapore oil products swaps were steady in a quiet market on Monday with gas oil prices continuing to slip in relation to jet fuel, traders said.
The jet fuel/gas oil regrade for February rose to $3.10/$3.20 per barrel up from this morning's $2.80 bid. March regrade also widened to $2.10/$2.40, from this morning's $1.80.

One trader attributed this to tight jet fuel supplies especially in light of the cuts in runs at three Singapore refineries and the shutdown of a crude unit at Mobil Oil Singapore since early last week.
Traders noted that gas oil swaps was offered lower despite a recovery seen on London's gas oil futures which last traded at $201.75 a tonne, up $1.75 from the previous close.
February gas oil on the International Petroleum Exchange had lost $8.00 a tonne to close at $200.00 on Friday.
February gas oil swaps was last quoted at $25.80/$25.90, with deals seen at $25.85 and $25.90. March was indicated at $26.10/$26.30.

Traders said the impact of India's top-up tender for March arrival on the market would be marginal as it seeks only two They said that due to a lack of regional demand, physical prices were expected to be lower than the deal done on Friday at $25.40 per barrel between a local trader and a Chinese trader.

Traders said fuel oil prices were more steady than gas oil. The physical fuel oil market would depend on how aggressively the major, which sold a cargo on Friday at $98.00 a tonne, would start offering later today.
Naphtha swaps was also largely unchanged.
